newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Executive Secretary Ruben Torres said yesterday proponents of the signature campaign for constitutional amendments are running out of time if they want a plebiscite held simultaneoulsy with the town elections on May 12 (STAR).

- The Palace yesterday defended its plan to renegotiate the controversial land deal in the Manila Bay reclamation area and said it may even go to court if the business consortium concerned refuses to change the terms of the transaction. (STANDARD/INQUIRER)
- The House of Representatives last night voted to drop the impeachment complaint against Ombudsman Aniano Desierto who was charged of graft. (CHRONICLE)

- A rebound in exports of electronics and components boosted the country's total exports in January to $1.688 billion, 18.8 percent higher than the $1.42 billion recorded in the same period last year. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Central Bank cut yesterday its overnight borrowing and lending rates following a drop in Treasury bill rates the previous day. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Fidel Ramos directed the departments of finance, budget and labour to "maximize efforts" to have tax breaks for individuals and corporations approved by the House of Representatives next week. (BUSINESSWORLD)
